title: Sell Mineral Rights in Wellsburg, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Wellsburg, WV | Brooke County Seat
metaDescription: Wellsburg is the Brooke County seat, and its courthouse holds the deed book that decides who owns the minerals under your tract. We research it and buy.
heroLead: Wellsburg sits directly on top of its own answer: the Brooke County Clerk's office here holds every deed, will, and lease that determines who actually owns a given mineral interest in this county.
intro: Being the county seat changes how we work a Wellsburg file. There's no courthouse commute or cross-county records request involved — the deed book, the fiduciary supervisor's estate index, and the lease record for most Brooke County tracts are all held in the same building, which lets us confirm a chain of title and answer an owner's question faster than in a county where records were split or moved.

That speed doesn't change what we look for. A Wellsburg mineral interest still needs its own title check: whether it was severed from the surface decades ago, whether an old lease is still binding it, and whether the interest passed cleanly to whoever is trying to sell it today.

sections.heading: The Brooke County Courthouse Record
paragraphs: Every mineral severance in Brooke County traces back to a deed recorded in this courthouse, some going back to the 1800s when a farmer sold or reserved the minerals under his land separately from the surface. That deed language, not the current property tax bill, is what governs ownership today.

We start there. If your family has owned a Wellsburg-area interest for generations, there's a good chance the last document referencing it by name is an old will or a lease memorandum, not anything with a modern owner's name attached.

sections.heading: Shallow Gas Under an Old River Town
paragraphs: Brooke County's production history runs mostly through shallow Gordon Sand and Big Injun wells drilled long before anyone in the Ohio Valley was talking about horizontal laterals. Some of those wells are still producing small amounts of gas today, and some were plugged decades ago with the lease never formally released from the record.
Either way, the mineral interest underneath is still a real asset, and its value depends on more than whether a well is currently pumping.

sections.heading: Flat-Rate Conversion Mechanics
paragraphs: A meaningful share of the older leases on file in Brooke County are flat-rate: a fixed yearly payment set decades ago, unrelated to how much gas the well actually produces. West Virginia law sets a 1/8 royalty floor, and a flat-rate lease that falls under it should be converted before an owner signs away the interest or accepts an offer based on the old payment structure.
We check this on every Wellsburg-area file, because a flat-rate lease and a properly converted royalty lease are not worth the same thing to a buyer.

sections.heading: Fragmented Ownership Along the Ohio
paragraphs: River-bottom and hillside farms in this part of Brooke County were often split among several children a hundred years ago, and those undivided fractions kept splitting with every generation that followed. It's common for us to find a Wellsburg mineral interest now held in a dozen small pieces by heirs scattered well outside West Virginia.
We buy those pieces individually. You don't need the rest of the family to agree or participate for us to make an offer on your share.

faqs.question: Since Wellsburg is the county seat, does that make the title research faster?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. The full Brooke County deed and estate record is kept in one office here, which lets us trace a chain of title without requesting records from another county.

faqs.question: Is my old flat-rate lease still legal?
faqs.answer: It can still be valid as written, but if it pays less than the state's 1/8 royalty minimum and there's relevant drilling activity, it may be entitled to convert. We check the lease language and the well status before we value your interest.

faqs.question: What if the mineral rights were never mentioned in my relative's will?
faqs.answer: That's common with older estates that were settled before anyone thought about the gas underneath. The interest usually still passed through the estate by operation of law, and we can trace it in the Brooke County record even if the will is silent on it.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests where multiple heirs each own a small piece?
faqs.answer: Yes. We regularly buy individual fractional shares from one heir at a time, without requiring the whole family to sell together.
